    Bug 1628441 - Render text body with unrecognized Content-Disposition inline. r=tobyp
    
    Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D295509

diff --git a/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser.toml b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser.toml
index 4806bd95e26..7ba0a42ce35 100644
--- a/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser.toml
+++ b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser.toml
@@ -37,6 +37,8 @@ support-files = ["data/**"]
 
 ["browser_imageOverflow.js"]

 ["browser_printing.js"]
 
 ["browser_untypedTextCteCharset.js"]
diff --git a/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser_malformedContentDisposition.js b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser_malformedContentDisposition.js
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..d4581a10cbe
--- /dev/null
+++ b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/browser_malformedContentDisposition.js
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+/**
+ * This Source Code Form is subject to the terms of the Mozilla Public
+ * License, v. 2.0. If a copy of the MPL was not distributed with this file,
+ * You can obtain one at http://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * Tests that a multipart/mixed message whose only text/plain part carries a
+ * malformed Content-Disposition (a Content-Transfer-Encoding value used as
+ * the disposition) still renders its body inline, instead of being hidden as
+ * an unnamed attachment.
+ */
+
+"use strict";
+
+var { open_message_from_file } = ChromeUtils.importESModule(
+  "resource://testing-common/mail/FolderDisplayHelpers.sys.mjs"
+);
+
+add_task(async function testMalformedContentDispositionRendersInline() {
+  const file = new FileUtils.File(
+    getTestFilePath("data/malformed_content_disposition.eml")
+  );
+  const msgc = await open_message_from_file(file);
+
+  Assert.ok(
+    msgc.content.document.body.textContent.includes(
+      "malformed Content-Disposition header"
+    ),
+    "body should render inline despite malformed Content-Disposition"
+  );
+
+  await BrowserTestUtils.closeWindow(msgc);
+});
diff --git a/mail/test/browser/message-reader/data/malformed_content_disposition.eml b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/data/malformed_content_disposition.eml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..f7a15eb31c4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/mail/test/browser/message-reader/data/malformed_content_disposition.eml
@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+Subject: Malformed Content-Disposition
+MIME-Version: 1.0
+Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="body-boundary"
+
+--body-boundary
+Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
+Content-Disposition: quoted-printable
+
+Body of a message whose only part carries a malformed Content-Disposition header.
+
+--body-boundary--
diff --git a/mailnews/mime/src/mimei.cpp b/mailnews/mime/src/mimei.cpp
index f2511854d11..59881b79831 100644
--- a/mailnews/mime/src/mimei.cpp
+++ b/mailnews/mime/src/mimei.cpp
@@ -842,9 +842,13 @@ MimeObject* mime_create(const char* content_type, MimeHeaders* hdrs,
    is ``inline'', then we display the part inline (and let mime_find_class()
    decide how.)
 
-   If there is any other Content-Disposition (either ``attachment'' or some
-   disposition that we don't recognise) then we always display the part as
-   an external link, by using MimeExternalObject to display it.
+   If the Content-Disposition is ``attachment'', we always display the part
+   as an external link, by using MimeExternalObject to display it.
+
+   Unrecognised values are treated as attachment per RFC 2183, except for
+   the first text part in the message, which falls back to inline so the
+   body is not hidden. This matches the observed behaviour of other e-mail
+   clients.
 
    But Content-Disposition is ignored for all containers except `message'.
    (including multipart/mixed, and multipart/digest.)  It's not clear if
@@ -942,7 +946,10 @@ MimeObject* mime_create(const char* content_type, MimeHeaders* hdrs,
                : 0;
   }
 
-  if (!content_disposition || !PL_strcasecmp(content_disposition, "inline"))
+  if (!content_disposition || !PL_strcasecmp(content_disposition, "inline") ||
+      (PL_strcasecmp(content_disposition, "attachment") &&
+       mime_subclass_p(clazz, (MimeObjectClass*)&mimeInlineTextClass) &&
+       opts && opts->state && !opts->state->first_part_written_p))
     ; /* Use the class we've got. */
   else {
     // override messages that have content disposition set to "attachment"
